title: The Small Light in the Hallway
passage:
The second floor of Aya's apartment building had a long hallway with three ceiling lights. All three stayed on from evening until morning. One of Aya's neighbors wondered whether so much light was necessary late at night, when very few people used the hallway. He suggested turning off two lights after midnight to save electricity.

The idea sounded reasonable, but another neighbor was worried about safety. She often returned from work after midnight and did not want the hallway to become dark. The building manager did not want to choose between saving energy and making people feel unsafe. Instead, he asked residents to test different lighting arrangements for one month.

During the first week, they turned off two lights after midnight. The hallway was still visible, but the ends were quite dark. Several residents said they did not like it. In the second week, they kept two lights on and turned off only the middle one. This was better, but the light was uneven. In the third week, the manager installed a small motion sensor near one of the lights. Two lights stayed on at a lower brightness, and the third became bright only when someone entered the hallway.

The residents preferred the third plan. People arriving late could see clearly, while the hallway used less electricity during quiet hours. The sensor was not expensive, but the manager still checked the electricity bill to make sure the change was useful. After two months, the building had used slightly less power than during the same period the previous year. The difference was small, yet the system was kept because residents also liked the softer light.

Aya found the process interesting. At first, the question had seemed simple: should the lights be on or off? The experiment showed that there were more choices between those two extremes. By testing several options, the residents found a solution that considered both energy use and safety. Aya learned that practical problems are often easier to solve when people stop arguing about only two choices and begin looking for a third one.
translation:
アヤの住む集合住宅の二階には長い廊下があり、天井灯が三つありました。三つとも夕方から朝まで点灯していました。ある住民が、深夜は通る人が少ないのだから二つ消して節電してはどうかと提案しました。

もっともらしい案でしたが、別の住民は安全を心配しました。仕事で真夜中を過ぎて帰ることがあり、暗い廊下は困るというのです。管理人は節電と安心のどちらか一方を選ぶのではなく、一か月間いくつかの照明方法を試すことにしました。

一週目は深夜に二灯を消しました。歩ける明るさは残りましたが、廊下の端がかなり暗くなり不評でした。二週目は中央だけ消す方法を試しましたが、明るさにむらが出ました。三週目、管理人は一つの照明に小さな人感センサーを付けました。二灯は低い明るさで点灯し、誰かが入ると三灯目が明るくなる仕組みです。

住民は三つ目の方法を最も気に入りました。遅く帰ってもよく見え、静かな時間帯の電力も減らせます。管理人は実際に効果があるか請求額も確認し、二か月後、前年同時期よりわずかに使用量が減っていました。差は大きくありませんでしたが、柔らかな明るさも好評だったため続けることになりました。

アヤにとって面白かったのは、最初は『つけるか消すか』だけに見えた問題に、その中間の選択肢があったことでした。いくつか試すことで、省エネと安全の両方を考えた方法を見つけられました。実際の問題では二つの案だけで争うより、第三の方法を探すことで解決しやすくなることがあると学んだのです。
